title: Detoxifying Language Models Risks Marginalizing Minority Voices

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing language model perplexity and conducting human evaluations of generation quality (topicality, fluency, and style) when the model is conditioned on African-American English (AAE) prompts versus White-Aligned English (WAE) prompts.

Measuring the increase in model perplexity on non-toxic text containing specific racial and ethnic identity mentions (e.g., 'blacks', 'mexicans', 'arab') to evaluate utility degradation caused by detoxification techniques.

bias_targets.target: Sexual orientation and Gender identity bias
bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model perplexity on non-toxic tweets containing LGBTQ+ identity mentions (e.g., 'gay', 'lesbian', 'transgender', 'non-binary') to assess disproportionate performance drops on marginalized groups.

Calculating model perplexity on text mentioning religious identities (e.g., 'muslim', 'jews') to determine if detoxification methods steer language models away from these topics due to spurious toxicity correlations.
